subject: Packaging & quantization: pilot economics and ops schedule
messages:
From: Jared Bloom <jbloom@finmetrics.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Asha Rao <asha.rao@finmetrics.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Oct 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Packaging & quantization: pilot economics and ops schedule

Kimberly / Karthik —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. FinMetrics is keen to run a six-week pilot of the Optimize toolkit across two product flows (inference for summaries and for downstream entity extraction). Before procurement jumps in, procurement asked for a concise economics and ops plan we can include in the SOW. Two things we need clarity on:

1) Quantization policy: can you confirm recommended quantization levels you’d advise for a throughput-focused pilot (we expect ~300 QPS peak, 35 tokens per request average)? Any guardrails around quality regressions we should budget for?

2) Credits / discounts: we have an internal approval path for credits versus committed spend. Would Redwood consider a blended approach (small upfront commit + credits tied to ops milestones)? If so, what are the typical bands and sample numbers you use for pilots this size?

I attached the excerpt from our RFP with the product flows called out (FinMetrics_RFP_Excerpt.pdf).

Can you send a short schedule (ops handoff, integration window, eval checkpoints) and a simple cost worksheet we can give to procurement?

Appreciate it — aiming to get Procurement looped and NDA signed this week.

—Jared
Jared Bloom
Head of Platform Engineering, FinMetrics
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Jared Bloom <jbloom@finmetrics.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 3 Oct 2025 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging & quantization: pilot economics and ops schedule

Jared —

Thanks for the RFP excerpt and the clear asks. High level answers first, then a one-page schedule below. I’m attaching a quick cost model (KP_cost_model_v2.xlsx) and a short quantization guidance doc (quant_guidance_short.pdf).

Quick answers:
- Quantization: for your latency/throughput profile, we recommend starting with 4-bit (QLoRA-style) of the served model family where supported; fallback to INT8 for parts of the pipeline that are sensitive to generation quality. We’ll include an eval run for the two flows to measure BLEU/EM/ROUGE-ish metrics and threshold quality delta (<2% absolute change on your key metric) before enabling full quantization in production.
- Credits/discounts: yes — we can do a blended pilot structure: small committed monthly baseline + milestone credits for successful go/no-go checkpoints. Typical bands for a pilot of this size: 10–20% on committed spend as pilot credit, scaling to 25–35% discount on committed annualized spend if you convert to Dedicated within 3 months. Exact structure depends on commit length and SLA expectations.

Proposed short schedule (six-week pilot):
Week 0: NDA + procurement intake + environment access (you)
Week 1: Integration kickoff, baseline metrics capture (Redwood + FinMetrics)
Week 2–3: Eval runs for quantization variants (4-bit, INT8) + cache policy tuning
Week 4: Quality gate review (we’ll run the shared eval set you provide)
Week 5: Load soak at projected peak QPS + ops runbook handoff
Week 6: Final report & mutual decision (go/no-go)

Next steps I suggest: 1) send expected traffic profile (p95 latency target, token distribution) — Jared, if you can confirm by Monday we’ll lock the eval plan; 2) procurement: we’ll share the SOW draft and a simple cost worksheet you can hand to procurement.

CC’ing Marcus to flag potential capacity questions; he’ll help with cost model assumptions.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Field Solutions — Redwood Inference
Attachments: KP_cost_model_v2.xlsx (cost worksheet), quant_guidance_short.pdf (short technical guidance)
From: Jared Bloom <jbloom@finmetrics.com>

Cc: Asha Rao <asha.rao@finmetrics.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 6 Oct 2025 08:54:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging & quantization: pilot economics and ops schedule

Kimberly —

Thanks, that schedule looks good. A couple of clarifications from procurement side:

- Our procurement team prefers credits for pilots rather than straight percentage discounts because of internal accounting treatment. Would Redwood be able to structure a $X credit drawdown tied to the three demo milestones (integration complete, quality gate passed, load soak passed)?
- SLA: for pilot we are OK with best-effort but procurement asked if any uptime target or priority queueing could be offered in the pilot to reduce false negatives during the eval; if that is an add-on we can discuss paid pilot support.

Also attached is a small spreadsheet with our projected token mix and QPS by flow (I’ll share that separately if procurement needs it). I can confirm the p95 latency target: <300ms for summaries, <400ms for extraction.

If you can send a one-page SOW draft + clause language you'd want for credits and rollback (in case quantization causes >2% metric regression), we’ll pass it to Procurement.

—Jared
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jared Bloom <jbloom@finmetrics.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 7 Oct 2025 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging & quantization: pilot economics and ops schedule

Jared / Kimberly —

Wanted to add a quick technical note on the eval mechanics and quantization guardrails so procurement and engineering are aligned:

1) Model variants: we’ll serve the open model family you previewed in the demo; for quantization experiments we’ll A/B runs with (a) FP16 baseline, (b) 4-bit quantized variant, and (c) INT8 as a compatibility fallback for specific ops. The A/B will be deterministic on the eval set to make delta measurement robust.

2) Quality gating: we’ll compute your agreed metric (you called out F1-ish for extraction and ROUGE-L for summaries) on the held-out set. Our gating rule: if quantized variant shows >2% absolute drop on either key metric, we roll back to FP16 for that endpoint.

3) Cache and batching: given 300 QPS peak, we recommend a two-tier cache: prefix-level reuse for long-lived prompts and a small in-memory KV cache for common user contexts. This reduces tokens billed and should improve throughput; we’ll instrument token-level billing in the cost worksheet so procurement can see the unit economics.

4) Pilot support & priority: we can provide a limited pilot SLA (4-hour response time on SEV2 during business hours) as a paid add-on. If Procurement needs priority queueing for the eval window, we can include it as a line item in the SOW.

I’ve attached a short note on quant tradeoffs (quant_guidance_short.pdf) and will coordinate with Marcus on cost assumptions.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal, Inference Optimization — Redwood Inference

Jared / Asha / Procurement —

Summarizing next steps so procurement has a single doc to reference:

1) SOW draft (attached: SOW_FinMetrics_v1.docx) — includes pilot scope, milestone-based credits ($25k credit split across integration/quality/load milestones), and optional pilot SLA line item ($6k flat for the 6-week window).
2) Cost worksheet (attached: KP_cost_model_v2.xlsx) — includes token mix assumptions, projected monthly spend at baseline FP16, and delta under quantized runs.
3) Eval & rollback clause — we’ll run the gating rule Karthik outlined; if the quantized variant degrades >2% on your agreed metric we automatically revert before production traffic.
4) Signatures: if you’re comfortable we can route the SOW + NDA for signatures (DocuSign link: https://docusign.com/envelope/ABC123-finmetrics-nda).

Proposed date for integration kickoff: Monday 13 Oct 2025 (gives both teams a week to review SOW and adjuments). If Procurement prefers an earlier start, flag it and we’ll try to compress Week 0 activity.

Marcus will follow up on the cost model assumptions and confirm the exact credit numbers if you’d like a different split than the $25k example above.

Happy to hop on a quick 30m call tomorrow to walk Proc through the SOW if that would speed things up.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Field Solutions — Redwood Inference
